faq.q: What is the origin of Hamisi?
faq.a: Hamisi is associated with Arabic. Hamisi is the Swahili form of Arabic خَامِس (Khāmis, 'fifth'), used for a child born on Thursday.
Yes — the underlying form خَامِس is Arabic.
Hamisi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hamisi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Khāmis is not a Quranic personal name.
